entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pekahiah, the seventeenth and third-from-last king of Israel, ruled from the capital of Samaria, succeeding his father Menahem. He was the second and last king of Israel from the House of Gadi, a sub-tribe of the Israelites. Pekahiah's reign began in 739 BCE and ended with his assassination, marking the end of the kingdom of Israel.

Pekahiah's significance lies in his role as the last king of Israel, a period marked by the Assyrian conquest of the northern kingdom in 722 BCE. His reign also saw the rise of the Assyrian Empire's influence in the region, which would shape the future of the Middle East.

The legacy of Pekahiah can be seen in the subsequent history of the region, including the Assyrian Empire's continued presence and the eventual rise of the Persian Empire. His reign also highlights the complexities of the Israelite monarchy, marked by internal power struggles and external threats.

In the annals of history, Pekahiah's story serves as a reminder of the transience of power and the enduring impact of historical events on the course of human civilization.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pekahiah's reign marked the end of the kingdom of Israel and paved the way for the Assyrian Empire's continued presence in the region, highlighting the complexities of the Israelite monarchy and the rise of the Assyrian Empire's influence in the Middle East.
